parts.note: Both 4x - 3y = 43. Checked: gradient of AB = 8/6 = 4/3; through (10,-1): 3(y+1) = 4(x-10) gives 4x - 3y = 43, and C satisfies it (40 + 3 = 43).

parts.note: Both 56 units^2. Checked: AC is horizontal (y = -1 at both ends), base 14, height 7 - (-1) = 8, area 56.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.note: Both 4/9. Checked two ways: SR parallel to OP with SR = (2/3)OP so triangles QSR and QOP are similar with area factor (2/3)^2; and by common heights (QS/QO)(QR/QP) = (2/3)(2/3) = 4/9.

key_verdict: Key and blind examiner agree on every part; all six values re-derived and confirmed, the area ratio by two independent routes.
fixes: The coordinate half is wholly routine: every exemplar's coordinate half carries an unknown to be found (k and p in 2024 Q3, a < 0 from a 25-unit length, p from a trapezium area in 2025 Q8), and this one has none. Replace (b) and (c) with one part that does: '(b) The point D has coordinates (2, k), where k < 0. The area of triangle ABD is 45 units^2. Find the value of k. [3]' (BD is vertical, length 7 - k; the perpendicular distance from A to the line x = 2 is 6; 3(7 - k) = 45 gives k = -8, the sign condition rejecting k = 22). The 6-8-10 length of AB is used nowhere afterwards and can go.

(d)(iii) asks the candidate to deduce SR parallel to OP, name the similar triangles and square the scale factor, for 1 mark; a real paper gives that deduction [2]. With (b) and (c) merged as above the marks are (a) 3, (b) 3, (d)(i) 2, (ii) 1, (iii) 2 = 11.
Key hygiene only (not paper-facing): the (d) line of the answer key repeats the three sub-answers that are then listed again as (d)(i)-(iii); print them once.
why: A genuine 4052 P2 shape (a coordinate-geometry half then an OPQ vector triangle with two 1:2 points ending in an area ratio) with clean exact numbers, correct register, part labels and a consistent figure, and its vector half re-skins none of the exemplars (the specimen ends in naming a quadrilateral, 2022 in a parallel-condition XD); it stops short of 5 because the coordinate half asks only for three direct computations with no unknown to find, and the one deduction that needs reasoning, (d)(iii), is under-weighted at 1 mark.
